note: Four separate questions in this archive now end at a door rather than a screen. This page is what somebody standing at each of those doors could settle, with the references written out so they do not have to be looked up again.

places.why: Six Booyzen estate files whose FamilySearch films refuse to serve images — film 007830063 and every film after it returns 403, and those are exactly the ones running to 1946 and later. A letter went on 13 September 2026 and has not been answered.

TAB MHG 3734/46
CATHERINE MARY SOPHIA DASCHNER, born BOOYZEN, b. 22 Apr 1891. HER NOTICE SHOULD NAME HER PARENTS — the most wanted page in this list.

JOHN BARRY BOOYZEN, b. c. 1884, who signed the 1905 Indwe form.

GERT JACOBUS BOOYZEN, b. 19 Jan 1870.

An index search, not a file

DAVID SCHALK BOOIJZEN (born Cradock, 9 June 1848) — alive and fifty-six at GOEDEHOOP, PRETORIA on 27 November 1905 and lost to this archive from that day. NO estate file and NO civil death can be found for him, and none for his second wife JOHANNA ELENA born STOLS, widow Lowies, either. If the Master's own estate index at Pretoria carries either of them, that is the answer. Their two known estate numbers are 4795 (his first wife, 1900) and 7081 (her first husband, 1905), so the pair were certainly known to that office.

THE SEVEN MARICO COMPENSATION CLAIMS, 1903–04. Read on the index today and they give nothing but initials: JPJ, PJ, GL, JPJ, L, JC, HE BOOYZEN. No forename, no farm, no amount, no remarks. THE INDEX LINE IS THE WHOLE RECORD and no screen anywhere will improve it. Seven thin files in one building. What is wanted from each is the claimant's full name, his farm and his field-cornetcy — enough to say whether any of the seven is this family. GL is the one to open first.
TAB OD — the Kwaggafontein school file, 1897–1900, and OR13059/97 with it

FORTY-EIGHT DOCUMENTS of one farm school in Marico, eight of them signed by a JGL BOOYZEN. What is wanted is his SIGNATURE and his FULL NAME — the head of a letter gives initials, the foot of one gives a name. OR262/98 (the subsidy application), OR6919/98 (the £61-6-0 deficit) and OR7499/99 (the £8 argument) are the three most likely to carry it. If he signs Jan Gerhardus Lodewicus, the man born 4 December 1855 stops being a blank.
TAB OD OR19199/98, OR19484/98 and OR2037/99 — Vaalbank, district Lichtenburg

THE SCHOOL ON THIS FAMILY'S OWN FARM. Its money papers are signed DS. BOOYSEN and DS BOOIJSEN. ONE QUESTION ONLY: is DS. a pair of initials — David Schalk — or the Dutch Ds., for dominee? One glance at a signature answers it. OR2037/99 is the letter about school materials for orphans and is the one worth copying whatever the answer.
places.note: The death notice from each is worth more than any one complete file. Six death notices beat one estate. 15 SEPTEMBER 2026 — PRETORIA ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS ABOUT BINDING. Ms Mavis Xaba, Archivist Assistant in the Reading Room, replied to the letter of 12 September: “ALL THE ESTATE FILES YOU ARE REQUESTING ARE BOUND FILES. UNFORTUNATELY, WE ARE THEREFORE UNABLE TO SCAN THESE FILES AND PROVIDE COMPLETE DIGITAL COPIES BY EMAIL.” She did not say any reference was wrong — including MHG 52653, the one this archive could not find on film. She put a private researcher who specialises in estate files on copy. THE DEPOT IS NOT REFUSING; THE PAPER IS SEWN INTO VOLUMES AND WILL NOT LIE ON A SCANNER. That is a physical fact about the record and it explains a great deal about what has and has not been filmed. Engaging the researcher is the user's decision and the user's money. 15 SEPTEMBER, LATER: written to. The researcher has been asked for her fees and her own view of whether these six files are worth the money, with an offer to begin with one. No payment details were sent and none will be.

places.why: SIX NATAL ESTATE FILES, and until today this archive had two. FamilySearch's filmed Natal probate series stops at 1950 and every one of these is later, so there is no screen that will ever show them. The address is now CHECKED against the repository's own entry. A letter is DRAFTED AND NOT SENT — requests/pietermaritzburg-archives-natal-estates.md. Four of the six were found on 14 September, two of them by learning who two women already in this archive's search log actually were.

KOLBE, FREDERIK FORTUNATUS HOFMEYR, born NAAUWPOORT, WAKKERSTROOM. The Settler's son's name in a fourth generation.
NAB MSCE 965/1956
KOLBE, HENDRIK JOHANNES HOFMEYR, born WAKKERSTROOM.
NAB MSCE 131/1959
BEUKES, PETRONELLA JACOBA ADRIANA, BORN KOLBE, BORN IN COLESBERG — now known to be the seventh of Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe's eight children, baptised at Colesberg 18 November 1877.
NAB MSCE 414/1960

OOSTHUIZEN, PIERRE FRANCOIS, born Colesberg, spouse ADRIANA HENRIETTA JOHANNA, BORN KOLBE — the youngest of the eight, baptised at Bethulie 23 October 1881. HER HUSBAND'S FILE, NOT HERS, so the page wanted is the one naming spouse and children.
NAB MSCE 2183/1958

BARRY, HENRY JAMES KOLBE, BORN IN BARKLY EAST, UNMARRIED. A Barry forename and a Kolbe surname in one man — and dying unmarried, his file should name parents or siblings rather than a widow. THE MOST WANTED PAGE IN THIS LIST.
NAB MSCE 600/1974
MOUNTJOY, CHRISTIAN, BORN IN BARKLY EAST, surviving spouse a Mountjoy.
NAB MSCE 581/1973 — SHOOTER, MATHILDA ELIZABETH, BORN MOUNTJOY, BORN IN BARKLY EAST

FOUND 15 SEPTEMBER, AFTER THE LETTER WAS DRAFTED. A SECOND Barkly East Mountjoy who died in Natal, alongside Christian Mountjoy already on this list. Barkly East is the town this family farmed in from about 1859, and two people leaving it for Natal is a pattern rather than an accident. Her death notice should name her parents.
NAB MSCE 21335/1934 — KOLBE, JOHANNA MARIA, BORN POTGIETER, spouse HENDRIK JOHANNES HOFMEYR KOLBE

THE WIFE OF A MAN ALREADY ON THIS LIST. MSCE 965/1956 is his; this is hers, twenty-two years earlier, and it gives him a wife's name and maiden surname this archive did not have. IF ONLY ONE OF THE TWO CAN BE COPIED, HERS IS EARLIER AND MORE LIKELY TO NAME HIS PARENTS.
NAB MSCE 8509/1923 and 15161/1929 — ELIZABETH JOHANNA KOLBE, BORN DU TOIT, and FREDERICK FORTUNATUS KOLBE

THE COUPLE THIS ARCHIVE DERIVED FROM BAPTISM REGISTERS, CONFIRMED FROM THE OTHER END. Frederik Fortunatus Kolbe, born Bethulie 1839, the Settler's tenth child, married Elizabeth Johanna du Toit — and both their estates are in Natal. His file is cross-referenced to hers in the index. WANTED: his death notice, which should name HIS parents and settle whether the Natal Kolbes descend from the Settler.
places.note: A seventh is worth adding if anyone is already in the building: NAB MSCE 4064/1974, BOOYZEN, NICOLAAS THEODORUS, BORN IN WAKKERSTROOM. This archive expects that to be a coincidence of surname and town and would like to be told so.

places.why: COMMANDANT JOHN GERSON ELIEZAR KOLBE died in the Orange Free State in 1868 leaving TWELVE CHILDREN, and this archive cannot name one of them. Two files in Bloemfontein would answer it. Neither is filmed and neither is name-indexed beyond the line quoted here.
asks: VAB MHG K71

KOLBE, JOHN GERSON ELEAZAR. Eggenote ANNA JACOBA (gebore VAN DER MERWE), 1868. The Settler's eldest son — Commandant of the district, J.P., director of the Bloemfontein Bank. THE DEATH NOTICE SHOULD LIST THE TWELVE CHILDREN.
VAB MHG M777

MCCABE, ANNA JACOBA, nooiensvan VAN DER MERWE, eggenote JOHN GHERSON [Kolbe], 1896. HIS WIDOW, UNDER HER SECOND HUSBAND'S NAME, twenty-eight years on. Her notice should name the same children as adults — which is better, because it would give their married surnames.
The Volksraad minutes for MAY 1867 — Notulen der Verrigtingen van den Hoogedelen Volksraad

HIS OWN WORDS, IF THEY WERE MINUTED. The Commandant's obituary says that on his deathbed he told the doctor and the others present THAT THIS STATE HAD TAKEN TOO MUCH LAND FROM THE BASUTOS, that he had always thought so AND HAD SAID SO IN THE RAAD, and begged them to rescind the resolution and treat with the Governor for an equitable boundary. If the May 1867 session minuted him, that is a man's political position in his own voice, a year before he died of a war he thought unjust. The printed Notulen are held here and are not online — HathiTrust has some years and is behind bot protection, and this archive will not go around that.
VAB estate of FRANCIS McCABE, Landdrost of Bloemfontein, d. 23 February 1872

THE OTHER WAY INTO THE TWELVE. He married the Commandant's widow about April 1871 and died fifteen months later leaving “a widow, four sons and two daughters, BESIDES A LARGE FAMILY OF STEP-CHILDREN”. Those step-children are the twelve. An executor listing them by name would answer from the opposite side to VAB MHG M777, which is not readable online. NAAIRS was down when this was raised and the reference has not been looked up.
VAB MHG C129 — FRANCIS McCABE, 1872, and VAB 1/3/1/12 BC11, his insolvent estate

C129 names both wives — MARIA PETRONELLA ELISABETHA ANTOINETTA RAATH and ANNA GEBORE VAN DER MERWE. WANTED: the heirs, and any list of children or step-children, which is the whole point. DO NOT TRAVEL FOR BC11: the index says outright “BEVAT GEEN STERFKENNIS NIE”, it contains no death notice, and the depot has saved somebody a wasted morning by writing it down.
VAB HG 4/2/1/1/456, 702/1931 — six Kolbes applying to the court together

LEONORA STEENKAMP born KOLBE · MARGARET DOWNING FICK born KOLBE · GEORGINA AUGUSTA DE WET born KOLBE · JACOBUS WYNAND LOUW KOLBE · GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE · CATHARINA ELIZABETH MALAN born KOLBE. SIX PEOPLE OF ONE SURNAME APPLYING TOGETHER IS A SIBLING GROUP, and applications like this are usually about a parent's estate — so the file should name the parent. THE FIRST FREE STATE KOLBE SIBLING GROUP THIS ARCHIVE CAN NAME AT ALL.
places.note: Also worth an hour while anyone is in the building: the Free State Volksraadsnotule for MAY 1867, the “corn peace”, in which he spoke against the boundary — and the farms LEEUWBERG, where he died, and KAALSPRUIT, where he settled about 1850 and lies.

asks: MOOC 8/18.11 — the inventory of GERRIT BOOIJSEN, 13 December 1781, Drakenstein

THE OLDEST DOCUMENT THIS FAMILY HAS, AND THE ONE IT OWES MOST. The index line names ELEVEN ENSLAVED PEOPLE of the household — Silvia, Lena, Sara, Janna, Dorinda, Fortuijn, Meij and Februarij van de Caab; Dijk and Farla van Madagascar; Achilles van Mallabaar. WANTED ENTIRE: every name and valuation on the list, and the HEIRS, because if the heirs include a Jan then this archive's direct line runs straight through this document. The TANAP transcription project put these inventories online and its database no longer resolves, so there is no screen route left. ALSO WANTED: MOOC 8/56.16a and 16b (Zacharias Booijsen, Graaff Reinet, 1805 and 1806), MOOC 8/42.46 (Aletta Booyzen, Graaff Reinet, 1820), MOOC 8/46.59 (Jan Lowies Booijsen, Onder Roggeveld, 1831) and MOOC 8/48.32 (Piet Booijsens, 1832).
SA LIBRARY, CAPE TOWN — MSB751, the GA Kolbe Collection (a library, not the archives)

FOUR PHOTOCOPIED PAGES, AND ONE OF THEM MAY BE THE LONDON ADDRESS. “GA KOLBE COLLECTION. Donated by Dr Jean Griffiths, Somerset West, 1985. Photocopy, 4 pages. George Augustus Kolbe, pharmacist, 1820 settler, MISSIONARY, married Margaret Downing. + LETTER, 1830 AUG. 23, FROM JOHAN KOLBE, LONDON, TO HIS SON, GEORGE AUGUSTUS KOLBE ON HIS ORDINATION.” WANTED: the letter, entire, and any address on it — this archive cannot decide between Brunswick Square and 34 Conduit Street and has exhausted the free directories. Also worth asking: where the ORIGINAL is, since this is a photocopy, and whether Dr Griffiths deposited anything else. NOTE THE BUILDING: this is the National Library of South Africa, not the Western Cape Archives, and it is a separate reader's ticket.
THE BAPTISM OF 21 SEPTEMBER 1788 — Petrus Jacobus Booijsen

THE SINGLE LINE THAT ENDS THE OLDEST QUESTION ON THIS SITE. De Villiers (1893) and de Villiers & Pama (1981) both place him under JAN Booijsen; the 1876 Rustenburg Sterfkennis names his father GERTHARDUS LÖDEWIKUS. De Villiers is not a source, he is an INDEX TO ONE — his entry was compiled from the Dutch Reformed baptism register. THE REGISTER ENTRY ITSELF names the father in a contemporary hand, written within days, by somebody with no reason to be confused. Congregation not yet established: the family is at Graaff-Reinet by 1812 but b3c4 Jan was a burgher at Drakenstein. Graaff-Reinet, Drakenstein and Stellenbosch doopregisters for September 1788 are the three to try, in that order.
JAMES MOUNTJOY's wills of 1818 and 1827, joint with ANNA CATHARINA SLIER. A Cape will of 1818 very often states where the testator came from, and every other document for this man leaves it blank.
A Colonial Office memorial of 1834 — “the widow of J Mountjoy, requesting remission of a fine”. A petition in her own voice.
The 1845 will of JOHANNA CATHARINA MONTJOY, made eighteen years before she died. Not name-indexed and not evidently filmed.
The 1866 liquidation account for her estate. It would divide it among eight children and give the daughters their married surnames.
The WAR LOSSES COMPENSATION COMMISSION, 1902

KAB, source NA, volume 564, reference A1068 onward. CATALOGUED BY SUB-COMMISSIONER, NOT BY CLAIMANT — so no search from outside the building can reach it. The question is whether any BOOYZEN or BARRY of Barkly East, Lady Grey or Wodehouse claimed. This is the burned-farm question, and it has never been properly asked.

WERDMULLER, COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO. DEATH NOTICE, 1882. THE PAGE THAT WOULD CLOSE THE WERDMULLER QUESTION: it lists his children, and would say whether CHARLES ANDREW is a son of AUGUSTA LOUISA KOLBE — and so whether a Victoria Cross married a great-granddaughter of the 1820 Settler.
WERDMULLER, AUGUSTA LOUISA (NEE KOLBE). DEATH NOTICE, 1873. The Settler's fourth daughter. Should name her children and her parents.
KOLBE, AUGUSTA LOUISA, WIFE OF COENRAAD JOHANNES OTTO WERDMULLER VAN ELGG. WILL, made 1868, filed 1873.
places.note: The compensation registers are the errand nobody can do remotely. Everything else on this list is a copy request.

asks: MANOROWEN

John Barry died here on 25 August 1903, aged 84, and was buried here. Harriet Louisa Barry, eighteen, was buried here in 1912. Margaretha Kolbe died here in 1915. THREE BURIALS IN TWELVE YEARS — is the ground still findable?
CHERRYVILLE and JERPOINT
The other two named Barry farms. Cherryville is where Harriet died of typhoid.
DUGMORE MINE, Indwe
Where a Booyzen worked underground in 1908. The only mine in this archive attached to a named member of this family.
The Indwe lidmaten and doop registers
Read here only through FamilySearch's index. The originals would settle what became of Willem Hermanus Booyzen after September 1910, when he vanishes at twenty-four.
Indwe cemetery
Johanna Catharina Mountjoy died here in June 1911 — the church register says so and the civil index does not have her.
places.note: Photographs of Manorowen, Cherryville and the Indwe workings would be the first images in this archive that are not of paper.

places.where: The National Archives, Kew — British Army records
places.addr: Bessborough Road, Richmond TW9 4DU, United Kingdom · nationalarchives.gov.uk · Reading rooms Tue–Sat, free, ticket required
places.why: THIS IS A NEW COUNTRY FOR THIS ARCHIVE AND IT IS HERE BECAUSE OF ONE SENTENCE IN A NEWSPAPER. John Montgomery, who lodged in his house at Cradock in January 1822, describes JAMES MOUNTJOY as “a saddler, WHO WAS DISCHARGED FROM THE 21ST LIGHT DRAGOONS”. James Montjoy's own death notice answers the question “names of the parents of the deceased” with NOT KNOWN, and his 1817 marriage register rules a line through the column that should say where he came from. Nobody at the Cape knew, because he did not arrive as a settler — he arrived in uniform. The army knew.
asks: WO 97 — Royal Hospital Chelsea, soldiers' documents, 21st Light Dragoons

THE DISCHARGE PAPER. Arranged by regiment for discharges before 1855. It gives the man's PARISH AND COUNTY OF BIRTH, his age at enlistment, his trade before enlisting, his service and the reason for discharge. A saddler born about 1782 and a civilian at the Cape by 1817 — he married at Graaff-Reinet on 9 March 1817 — should be discharged in the years either side of that. ONE PAGE ENDS A QUESTION THIS SITE HAS CARRIED AS BLOCKING SINCE IT WAS WRITTEN.
WO 12 — muster books and pay lists, 21st Light Dragoons

If the discharge paper is not there, the musters will show when he ceased to appear and where the regiment was. They also carry trade and sometimes birthplace. The regiment was the cavalry of the Cape garrison from the 1806 expedition; its Cape musters are the years to read.
Anything on the regiment's disbandment at the Cape

Men discharged at the Cape rather than shipped home are the ones who stayed and married into the colony. If there is a list of them, James Mountjoy should be on it — and so, probably, should several other names this archive has met without explanation.
places.note: NOT YET WRITTEN TO AND NOT YET COSTED. Kew's copying service and its independent-researcher list are both online. This is the first errand this archive has had outside South Africa.
